one_liner: Twenty is an open-source CRM with REST and GraphQL APIs, OAuth 2.0 with self-serve dynamic client registration, API keys, and an official MCP server. Builders can get credentials from a free self-hosted instance or a cloud trial.
auth_notes: Authorization code + PKCE and client credentials. Clients register programmatically via RFC 7591 at POST /oauth/register, with no dashboard approval. API keys are Bearer tokens created in Settings → Developers → API. Each workspace has its own base URL.
access_notes: The cloud plan needs a trial or a paid plan. A 30-day trial needs a card, and a 7-day trial needs no card, per a third-party directory. Self-hosted Twenty is free with all Pro features, so a developer can get working API credentials at no cost. Cloud API access starts at Pro, about $9–12/user/month.
blocker_notes: There is no real blocker. The free self-hosted edition or a 30-day cloud trial is enough to build and test. The API schema is per workspace and includes custom objects, so the toolkit should discover the schema at runtime.

evidence.quote: Twenty implements OAuth 2.0 with authorization code + PKCE for user-facing apps and client credentials for server-to-server access.
Twenty supports **dynamic client registration** per [RFC 7591](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591). No manual setup needed — register programmatically:
Create an API key in **Settings → Developers → API → + Create key**. Copy it immediately — it’s shown once.
Self-hosted Free: $0 with all Pro features (community support). No free cloud plan.
the pricing page says '30-day trial... without credit card', but in the app (2026-10-25) the 30-day trial needs a card
**Core API** — `/rest/` and `/graphql/` CRUD on records: People, Companies, Opportunities, your custom objects.
The REST base is `https://{your-workspace-url}/rest`, with per-workspace OpenAPI at `/rest/open-api/core` and `/rest/open-api/metadata`
Twenty exposes an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server so that AI assistants — Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, and others — can read and write your CRM data
